Selections & results journal

Lock a snapshot before the race. Later, enter the official 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th finishers to compare your recorded rankings. Remove mistaken entries using the row button or selected-entry control; undo restores the last removal during this session. Demo records are excluded from real-race summaries.

Methods, assumptions & limitations

Race Analyzer 3.0: four complementary approaches produce one top four: independent Speed, Pace, Finishing and Class/Form views; controlled/balanced/heavy-pressure scenarios; all-pairs comparisons; and automatic synthesis. This is a deterministic rule system, not a trained prediction model or a win-probability estimate. Historical model training (approach 5) is deferred.

Manual top-four removal: click Remove from top four, enter one optional reason and apply. The next eligible horse moves into the recalculated selections. The removed horse stays active for pace, Fulcrum, speed benchmark and field comparisons. Restore to consideration reverses the removal. Reasons are included in journal snapshots and CSV exports; Save session JSON retains live overrides. Fewer than four eligible runners produces fewer than four selections.

Automatic lines and compact override: Auto starts with up to three original PP slots. Each qualifying source line in L1–L3 adds one older slot, even if several reasons occur on that line. A significant class drop can add one more. Maximum L10 or the last supplied slot. The explanation names the source and added slot. Choose Lines 1–10 beside any horse to replace Auto; Reset removes that override. The one limit applies to that horse’s factors, PPF and Fulcrum. Date and comparability checks still apply. Old per-factor and single-PPF-line overrides are ignored. Explicit horse-wide limits from older sessions are retained.

Extension reasons: a recent line on a different dirt/turf/synthetic surface from today; sloppy or muddy dirt (sy/my), soft or yielding turf (sf/yl); a recent sprint when today is a route, or a recent route when today is a sprint (route = 8f or longer). These reasons do not require a poor finish, and unknown surface, condition or distance does not trigger them. These use the same L1-L3 extension rule above. Other reasons: surprise pace = led/within 1L at 2C but not in the immediately preceding race; surprise ITM = 1st–3rd after two races outside the money; close at both calls while dropping class today; Fast Five = small BRIS 2C shape ≥+5 and close at both calls; a 45+-day layoff return close at 2C; positive second/third off a layoff = finish within 4¾L plus maintained speed at same/higher class or close at both calls. “Close” is ≤2¾L in sprints, ≤4¾L in routes. Unknown evidence does not trigger a reason. Significant drop = at least 25% lower claiming price at the same claiming/optional-claiming level, or allowance/optional claiming to claiming.

Post-position profile: exact track, surface, distance and about-distance match; current chart-meet sample. Uses actual gate position from Single File or your Post entry; PDF program numbers are not gate positions. Each starter contributes 1/field-size expected wins. Wins/expected at least 1.20 = Favorable (+2 in pace comparisons); at most 0.80 = Unfavorable (-2); otherwise neutral. Requires 30 races and 20 starts from the post, with no future sample dates. No automatic gate renumbering after scratches; verify Post when gates change. Bundled post samples cover charts through October 18, 2026; later files in your folders have not been processed into these profiles. Imported post data takes precedence; older style-only JSON retains the labeled bundled post fallback. Download current profile data exports both style and post statistics. Post and running-style adjustments are small comparison aids, not probabilities.

Class hierarchy: Grade 1 (9), Grade 2 (8), Grade 3 (7), Stakes (6), Handicap (5), Allowance/Optional claiming (4), Starter allowance (3), Claiming (2), Maiden claiming (1). Maiden special weight is outside scope and receives no top-four selections. Proven class means a comparable line with a finish within 4¾L. The best proven tier is used; merely entering a higher race is insufficient. Purse, claim and printed conditions are displayed; purse does not override the hierarchy. Within claiming levels a price difference of at least 25% is significant. Unknown types stay unclassified.

Form: use the latest two or three comparable numeric figures inside the allowable window. Improvement = +2 points from the preceding qualifying figure, or three strictly rising figures, or newly close at both calls; supporting efforts must finish within 4¾L at the same or higher class. Maintaining = speed change under 2 points, same hierarchy and qualifying finishes. Declining = at least 2 points lower, or weakening early involvement and finish, against no stronger class. Otherwise Mixed/Insufficient evidence. Higher figures after a class drop alone are not improvement. The source slots are visible.

Dirt win-contender designation: benchmark is the second-highest of active horses’ original L1 speed figures, counting ties. At least two valid latest figures are required. Within original L1–L3, independently of the factor limit, require a speed figure ≥ benchmark and a finish 1st–3rd or strictly under 2L behind. These can be different lines. Uncertain evidence is labeled Unproven/Unavailable. The date-age limit applies. Turf and synthetic do not use this dirt test. It does not filter the final top four.

Sheet patterns (3.8): from the Marching notes, read from BRIS speed figures in the horse's last 10 races (1 BRIS point counts as 1 sheet point). Marching: 2 or more new lifetime Bests in the last 4 races, and the last race within 5 points of the Best. Circle back: the Best was 2 or more races ago and the horse is coming back to it; tight means an off race 4+ points slower and now within 2 of the Best, loose means slower races and the last one turned back up. Rest then best: a new Best in the 1st or 2nd race back from a 60+ day layoff, within the last 2 races. Hover a tag for the numbers. These are labels only and do not change the ranking. In the 284-race backtest none of them picked more winners; horses ranked 2nd to 4th that were Marching returned $1.13 per $1 (125 horses, 27 winners), which may be luck, so the journal records each tag with the horse's rank (for example march+rest_best@3).

Watch at odds (3.7): a horse ranked 5th or lower is labeled Watch at odds when it has one of the two best BRIS early pace figures (best of its last 3 races) among today's runners, its morning line is under 15-1, and it is not switching to turf. In the 286-race backtest these horses won 16 of 112 starts (14%), compared with 44 of 1,088 (4%) for the other horses ranked 5th or lower. Most of that edge came from the earlier dates, so the journal tracks how the label does going forward. It is a price play, not a pick.

Best tickets (3.11): the app turns its ratings into win chances, then ranks exacta and trifecta combos by how likely they are (Harville method, with second and third place chances flattened a little because favorites run second less often than their win chance suggests). Each ticket shows its chance and a fair $2 payout with no takeout. If the will-pay on your betting site is higher, the ticket is value. In the 285-race backtest the top 6 exactas hit 36% and the top 12 trifectas hit 20%. On early dates it tied boxing the top horses; on later dates it did better. Payouts were not tested. It does not change the rankings.

Contender list (3.10): horses ranked in the top 4 when 8 or fewer run, or in the top 6 when 9 or more run, get a green Contender tag. In the 286-race backtest the winner came from this list in 87% of races (86% on early dates, 87% on later dates), with 4.8 horses on average; a plain top 4 caught 79%. It does not change the rankings. Use it to choose which horses to bet by their odds.

Version 3.6 rating: the final order sorts horses by one rating. Each input is scored against today's field (how far above or below the field average it is), then weighted: morning line 0.6, Prime Power 0.3, best-two speed average 0.15. A missing value counts as the field average. The head-to-head net score below is still shown and breaks exact ties. Settings are in RA_TUNING.

Version 3.5 tuning: each comparison first checks BRIS Prime Power. A horse more than 2 Prime Power points higher wins the pair. When the two are within 2 points, or either is missing Prime Power, the race-specific order below decides. The class and speed precedence rules described below are switched off in 3.5 because a 286-race backtest found they lowered accuracy. Settings are in RA_TUNING.

Comparison tolerances: speed differences ≤2 points and PPF differences ≤0.20 equivalent-2f seconds are ties. Same class tier is tied; finishing mean beaten-length differences ≤0.75L, pace-fit differences ≤5 points and connections-rate differences ≤3 percentage points are ties. These implementation thresholds are working assumptions, not validated statistical limits. Unknown values never become zeros or automatic losses.

Protection against a pace-only upset: a significant proven class advantage (two hierarchy levels, or a 25% claiming-price difference at the same claiming tier) takes precedence when its speed is within 5 points of the opponent. A clear speed advantage over 2 points takes precedence at class within one tier, except turf routes where speed primarily confirms competitiveness. For ordinary class comparisons a horse more than 5 speed points slower cannot win on class alone. Proven Grade 1–3 class moves first in the race-specific order, subject to this speed-competitiveness check.

Race-specific priorities: ordinary dirt sprint: speed → pace → form → class → connections → PPF. Pressured sprint: speed → pace → finishing/PPF → form → class → connections. Dirt route: speed/distance ability → pace → proven class → form → PPF → connections; pressure moves PPF ahead of Form but after proven class. Turf sprint: speed → pace → form/finish → class → PPF → connections, with PPF promoted under pressure. Turf route: proven class → finishing/PPF → form → tactical pace → competitive speed range → connections. Synthetic uses explicitly labeled dirt-like ordering pending its own rules. “Distance proof” is a comparable finish within 4¾L at a distance within half a furlong of today.

Views and final order: each viewpoint compares horses using only its evidence. The working pace comes from projected styles and Quirin: two E horses or three E/EP with Q≥5 = pressure; one E without another EP Q≥5 = controlled; otherwise balanced/uncertain. Compare every active pair using the race priorities, stopping at the first meaningful difference. Rank by net wins minus losses. Equal totals use top-four placement across scenarios, number of top-three viewpoint supports, number of comparable speed lines, repeated competitive class lines, then connections. Program order breaks a remaining display tie; “Closely matched” remains visible. Circular pair preferences can occur. Scenario ranks are stress tests, not assigned likelihoods. Shared evidence is not added as four independent weighted scores.

Evidence availability: the display counts available Speed, Pace, Class, Trainer, Jockey and PPF fields out of six, not confidence. At least four active horses yields four displayed choices even with limited evidence; MSW is the exception. Trainer/jockey rates = (wins+2)/(starts+20) ×100, using supplied counts; PDF meet versus Single File year stats can differ. Both rates must be available for a combined connections tiebreak.

Comparable lines: same dirt/turf/synthetic family, same sprint/route category (routes ≥8f), within 1f, inside the maximum race age and not future-dated. Outside turf routes, Speed = equal thirds of the mean of all qualifying figures, best-two mean and best-three mean. Each uses the same horse-specific allowable comparable lines; fewer than two or three uses available lines. With one or two lines all three means coincide; zero lines means unavailable. These overlapping measures are not independent evidence. Click Speed for components, source lines and qualifying count. Top-three component designations are informational only and do not change ratings or rankings. Rank is one plus the number of unscratched horses with a strictly higher component value; ties share rank and missing figures are unranked. Scratches recalculate designations; manual top-four removals remain in the active field. One- or two-line evidence is flagged as repeated evidence. The separate dirt latest-race/last-three benchmark is unchanged. Turf-route speed competitiveness uses the displayed range high. The custom range uses numeric allowed figures: 2–5 = second-worst to best; 6–8 = third-worst to second-best; 9–10 = fourth-worst to third-best. A single figure is displayed alone. Median speed uses all numeric figures eligible for this range within the horse-specific allowable lines and date limit, before range trimming. It is the middle sorted figure, or the average of the two middle figures for an even count. It is informational only and does not affect ranking.

PPF: select lowest normal PPF in the window. PPF = (final race time − 2C race time + 0.20 × finish BL) × 2 / remaining furlongs. Normal values take precedence. Only when none is available, use lowest valid same-surface distance extrapolation: 6.3 seconds per half-furlong for sprints, 6.4 for routes, adjusting both final distance and call location. Missing fractions cannot be fabricated. In comparisons, PPF requires a competitive finish from each selected PPF line. It is secondary in ordinary sprints, promoted under heavy pressure, more useful in dirt routes, and central with class/finishing in turf routes. No stars or late-call projector.

Projector and Fulcrum: use median horse call times (race time +0.20 × BL) over allowed paired-call lines. Relative gaps determine E=leader, EP≤2L, P>2–5L, S>5L. Fulcrum takes projected E/EP runners’ newest eligible comparable early/competitive line, skipping two documented excuses; first-call BL≤2, second/finish BL≤5. Benchmark = fastest 2C +0.20 ×2C BL. Fallback 45.2s at 4f for 5.5–7f; 71.8s at 6f above 7f. Races over 7f below 8f use the fallback to avoid mismatched calls. Scratches recalculate everything.

Fulcrum handling and profiles: a test uses raw race 2C ≤ Fulcrum, same call distance; win/finish within 5L is competitive. Demonstrated≥2, Some evidence=1, Concern≥2 failed tests with no success, otherwise Unproven or Unavailable. Exact track/surface/distance style profile: full weight (±3) needs 30 complete races and 20 style starters from the current meet; a limited sample (at least 15 races and 10 starters) counts at reduced weight (±2) and is labeled; when the current meet is thinner, the all-history set (at least 15 / 10) is blended two thirds current meet and one third history, labeled, at reduced weight; wins/field-expected≥1.20 favorable, ≤0.80 unfavorable. Profile evidence can make a small pace adjustment, never supersede a major speed/class advantage. No future-dated profiles are used.

PDF and storage: text-layer BRISNET Ultimate PP layout only, tested with bel1022u.pdf. Review is optional; validation still runs. Horse-name clicks open the original PDF at its verified heading; a matching PDF must be attached. No PDF bytes are stored in session JSON. Notes, overrides, selections and imported data are. Download session backups; browser storage alone is not a portable backup. The app is offline and uses explicit rules, not a live AI service. Raw times have no daily/intertrack variants; no guarantees of accurate pace or profitable bets.
